newsitem.title: USA: U.S. opposes use of force to reverse S. Leone coup.
newsitem.headline: U.S. opposes use of force to reverse S. Leone coup.

text.p: The United States said on Friday it would oppose any use of force by Nigerian-led West African peace-keeping troops to overturn last Sunday's military coup in Sierra Leone.

Asked if the Nigerians should use force to restore democratic government in Sierra Leone, State Department spokesman John Dinger told reporters: "There is no need. We would oppose any further violence."

Dinger spoke as Nigeria flew in troops, jeeps and armoured personnel carriers for an expected regional intervention to restore President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah. There were signs that Ghana and Guinea would join in.

Dinger said Washington had made its views known to Nigeria. "We are using all possible diplomatic channels, both directly to the coup leaders in Sierra Leone, but also to our allies in the region and elsewhere to try to get them to urge the restoration of the civilian government in Sierra Leone," he said.
"We will continue to pursue all diplomatic efforts, including all international pressure possible, to restore the democratically elected government in Sierra Leone," Dinger added.
"There has been enough violence in Sierra Leone. We hope democracy is quickly restored there by diplomatic means and through international pressure."
